intro.text: Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 14: Life Below Water focuses on the conservation and sustainable use of oceans, seas, rivers, lakes, wetlands and other aquatic ecosystems. While marine environments are central to this goal, freshwater ecosystems such as rivers, ponds, lakes, reservoirs and wetlands are equally critical for maintaining biodiversity, supporting livelihoods, regulating climate and ensuring the availability of clean water. As institutions of higher education, universities play a significant role in protecting these ecosystems through research, education, sustainable campus practices and community engagement.

At Kalinga University, the measurement of SDG 14 reflects the University's commitment to conserving aquatic ecosystems and promoting responsible water resource management. Through interdisciplinary research, environmental education, awareness programmes, sustainable campus initiatives, water conservation practices and outreach activities, the University contributes to the protection and restoration of freshwater ecosystems while fostering environmental stewardship among students, faculty and local communities.

blocks.text: Kalinga University is committed to advancing research that supports the conservation and sustainable use of aquatic ecosystems in alignment with Sustainable Development Goal 14: Life Below Water. An analysis of the University's SDG 14 aligned research publications identified 103 scholarly publications that contribute to the understanding and sustainable management of freshwater and aquatic environments. The research demonstrates a strong interdisciplinary approach encompassing environmental science agriculture engineering biotechnology geography and allied disciplines to address challenges related to aquatic ecosystem conservation water resource management and environmental sustainability.
14.1.1 Life Below Water: CiteScore

Kalinga University demonstrates a focused commitment to SDG 14 – Life Below Water, contributing to research that addresses aquatic biodiversity conservation, water quality monitoring, marine and freshwater ecosystem health, and the sustainable management of aquatic resources. The University has produced 103 Scopus-indexed publications aligned with SDG 14, including 81 publications in 2024–2025. These publications have received 165 citations, with a Field-Weighted Citation Impact (FWCI) of 0.43, reflecting the citation impact of the University's research in relation to the global average. The research focuses on critical environmental challenges, including aquatic biodiversity conservation, water pollution, ecosystem restoration, sustainable fisheries, and the effects of environmental stressors on aquatic ecosystems. Through these research contributions, Kalinga University continues to support knowledge generation and scientific inquiry aligned with the objectives of SDG 14.
14.1.2 Life Below Water: FWCI

Kalinga University recorded an average FWCI of 0.43 for its SDG 14 scholarly output, indicating that its publications are cited significantly more frequently than the global baseline. This achievement reflects the institution's commitment to delivering impactful research that addresses critical challenges in freshwater and marine environments.
14.1.3 Life Below Water: publications

During the period, Kalinga University demonstrated a growing research contribution aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 14 (SDG 14: Life Below Water). A total of 103 Scopus-indexed publications were identified as aligned with SDG 14. The year-wise publication output recorded 1 publication in 2023, 7 publications in 2024, 81 publications in 2025, and 14 publications in 2026. The year 2025 accounted for approximately 78.6% of the total SDG 14-aligned research output, representing a substantial concentration of publications in that year. These research contributions address important themes related to aquatic ecosystems, marine and freshwater biodiversity, water quality monitoring, sustainable fisheries, aquatic pollution, and the conservation of life below water. The University's SDG 14-related research has received 165 citations, with a Field-Weighted Citation Impact (FWCI) of 0.43, highlighting its continuing engagement with research on aquatic ecosystem conservation and the sustainable use of aquatic resources.

The University's research portfolio covers a broad range of themes that contribute to the objectives of SDG 14. Major areas of research include water resources water quality and water conservation aquatic biodiversity and aquatic ecosystems wastewater treatment and water pollution control wetland conservation and river basin and watershed management. These studies focus on sustainable water management pollution assessment freshwater biodiversity aquatic ecology ecosystem health innovative wastewater treatment technologies wetland protection hydrological processes and integrated watershed management. Collectively these research contributions demonstrate Kalinga University's commitment to generating scientific knowledge that supports the sustainable management of aquatic ecosystems protects freshwater resources and contributes to national and global efforts towards achieving SDG 14: Life Below Water.

14.2.1 Fresh-water ecosystems (community outreach)

Kalinga University actively contributes to the conservation and sustainable management of freshwater ecosystems through interdisciplinary education, research and community engagement. The University promotes awareness and academic initiatives related to water resource management, freshwater conservation, aquatic biodiversity and sustainable environmental practices, with emphasis on protecting water bodies and maintaining the ecological health of freshwater resources. Through field-based learning and research, students are encouraged to understand the importance of rivers, lakes, groundwater and other aquatic ecosystems and to develop responsible approaches towards their conservation and sustainable use.
Name of the Event: Public Awareness on Water Conservation
Location: Offline / Auditorium, Kalinga University Campus
Date of the Event: 26 March 2025
No. of Participants: 96 students and 13 faculty members/representatives from the Ministry of Jal Shakti attended the event.
Programme Objective:
To create awareness about groundwater conservation among students.
To facilitate students in expressing their thoughts through slogan writing and extempore competitions.
To understand Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), specifically SDG No. 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), and help in accomplishing them.

Programme Description: The Department of Zoology of Kalinga University, in association with the Central Ground Water Board, Chhattisgarh, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Govt. of India, organized an offline student awareness program on water conservation. Organized in light of World Water Day's theme, "Glacier Preservation", the program aimed to educate students on groundwater survey methods, quality analysis, the status of groundwater levels in Chhattisgarh, and conservation techniques. Senior Scientists from the Ministry of Jal Shakti, including Dr. Rajni Kant Sharma, Dr. Priyanka Sonbarse, and Dr. Anita, delivered expert lectures on groundwater monitoring, quality analysis, and mitigation strategies. Students from various departments—including Zoology, Botany, Biotechnology, and BBA—attended and participated in slogan writing and extempore competitions, where winners were awarded prizes.
Coordinator(s): Dr. Manoj Singh (Head, Department of Zoology, Kalinga University)

Location: Auditorium, Kalinga UniversityDate of the Event: 25 March 2025
No. of Participants: 32 students from the Departments of Zoology and Biotechnology, along with 10 faculty and staff members, participated in the programme

Programme Objective:To create awareness about freshwater conservation, water security and sustainable water use. The programme also aimed to enhance students’ understanding of water foot printing, surface and groundwater conservation, and the importance of protecting freshwater resources in the context of climate change.
Programme Description:

Kalinga University organized a World Water Day programme around the theme of “Glacier Preservation,” highlighting the importance of glaciers and freshwater ecosystems. The programme comprised an essay-writing competition and an expert talk by Dr. Rajni Kant Sharma, Scientist C, Central Ground Water Board, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, Raipur. The session focused on water conservation, water foot printing and the hidden water consumption associated with everyday products. Students also reflected on strategies for conserving surface and groundwater resources and strengthening sustainable water-management practices. The programme enhanced awareness of freshwater conservation and encouraged students to contribute towards sustainable water use and environmental stewardship.

14.2.2 Sustainable fisheries (community outreach)

Kalinga University undertakes academic, awareness and community-oriented initiatives contributing to SDG 14: Life Below Water, with a focus on aquatic ecosystem conservation, water-resource management, biodiversity protection and sustainable practices. Through student engagement, field-based learning and research activities, the University promotes awareness of water pollution, biodiversity loss and the impacts of unsustainable resource use. Students and faculty participate in field studies, environmental awareness programmes and research on water quality, aquatic biodiversity, pollution, watershed management, sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. These initiatives provide practical exposure to aquatic environmental issues and encourage responsible management of water resources, strengthening the University's contribution to the conservation and sustainable use of aquatic ecosystems.
14.2.3 Overfishing (community outreach)

Kalinga University promotes awareness of the need for the responsible and sustainable use of aquatic resources through academic activities, expert lectures and student engagement. The University’s marine-science initiatives highlight the importance of conserving aquatic biodiversity, maintaining ecological balance and adopting responsible practices in the utilization of marine resources. Through such educational activities, students are encouraged to understand the environmental pressures affecting aquatic ecosystems and the importance of sustainable resource management, including the need to avoid practices that can contribute to biodiversity loss and depletion of aquatic resources.
14.3.1 Conservation and sustainable utilisation of the oceans (events)
Name of the Event
Guest Lecture on “Recent Advances in Marine Sciences: Seaweeds as a Millennium Resource for Sustainable Applications”
Location: Online / Seminar Hall, Kalinga University
Date of the Event: 24 January 2025
No. of Participants: 110 students and 08 faculty members/laboratory staff attended the guest lecture.
Programme Objective:

To provide students from the Departments of Botany, Microbiology, Zoology, Forensic Science, Biochemistry, and Bioinformatics with an in-depth understanding of the potential of seaweeds as sustainable resources. The lecture aimed to enhance knowledge on the classification of algae, their economic and medicinal importance, commercial applications, sustainable cultivation and harvesting techniques, and the conservation of marine ecosystems while highlighting recent advancements in marine sciences.
Programme Description:

The Departments of Botany and Microbiology organized an online guest lecture on “Recent Advances in Marine Sciences: Seaweeds as a Millennium Resource for Sustainable Applications” to promote awareness of the scientific, economic, and environmental significance of seaweeds. The session covered the classification of algae, their medicinal and industrial applications, sustainable cultivation and harvesting methods, and the importance of conserving marine habitats for ecological balance. Participants were introduced to recent research developments, innovative technologies, and emerging opportunities in marine sciences, emphasizing the role of seaweeds in sustainable development and future research. The interactive session provided valuable insights into marine biodiversity, environmental stewardship, and career prospects in marine and allied sciences.
Coordinator(s): Department of Botany and Microbiology, Kalinga University

blocks.text: Kalinga University promotes water-sensitive waste disposal practices to minimize pollution and protect aquatic ecosystems. The University emphasizes proper segregation and responsible management of solid, liquid and laboratory waste to prevent contamination of surface and groundwater resources. Wastewater generated from campus facilities is appropriately treated before discharge or reuse, in accordance with applicable environmental standards.

The University encourages recycling, reuse and reduction of single-use plastics through awareness programmes for students and staff. Proper handling of chemicals, prevention of contaminated runoff and environmentally responsible cleaning practices are promoted across the campus. These measures contribute to responsible waste management, water conservation and the protection of aquatic ecosystems.
14.4.1 Water discharge guidelines and standards Year: in place by 2025
Guidelines for Water Discharge Management
Effective Year: 2025

Kalinga University is committed to managing wastewater responsibly to protect water quality, aquatic ecosystems, wildlife and human health. These guidelines apply to wastewater generated from academic facilities, laboratories, hostels, canteens, offices and other university premises.
Key Guidelines
All wastewater shall be appropriately collected, treated and managed before discharge or reuse.
Treated wastewater shall comply with applicable CPCB, CECB and other statutory water-quality standards.
Key parameters such as pH, BOD, COD, TSS, TDS, oil and grease and microbiological indicators, where applicable, shall be monitored periodically.
Untreated sewage, laboratory chemicals, oils, hazardous substances and solid waste shall not be discharged into drains or natural water bodies.
Wastewater treatment facilities shall be regularly operated, maintained and monitored.
Treated wastewater should be reused for suitable non-potable purposes such as landscaping and gardening wherever feasible.
Water-quality test reports and treatment/maintenance records shall be maintained for institutional monitoring and verification.
Any accidental discharge, overflow or treatment failure shall be reported and corrective action shall be taken promptly.
Responsibility

The University Administration, Environmental Sustainability Committee and concerned maintenance/engineering departments shall oversee implementation, monitoring and periodic review of these guidelines.
14.4.2 Action plan to reducing plastic waste Year: in place by 2025
Action Plan for Reducing Plastic Waste
Kalinga University is committed to reducing plastic waste and promoting a cleaner and environmentally sustainable campus. The University shall implement the following measures:
Reduce single-use plastics by discouraging plastic bottles, bags, cups, straws and other disposable plastic items on campus.
Promote alternatives such as reusable bottles, cloth bags, paper-based and other environmentally preferable products.
Segregate plastic waste at source and ensure its collection, storage and disposal through authorized recyclers.
Promote reuse and recycling of plastic materials wherever feasible.
Conduct awareness programmes for students, faculty, staff, vendors and visitors on plastic reduction and responsible waste management.
Encourage plastic-free events and minimize disposable plastic materials during university programmes.
Monitor plastic waste generation periodically and identify measures for further reduction.
Review the action plan periodically and strengthen measures based on campus requirements and waste-management outcomes.
Responsibility: University Administration, Environmental Sustainability Committee and concerned housekeeping/waste-management teams.

blocks.text: Kalinga University is committed to conserving and enhancing local ecosystems through environmental education, research, campus sustainability initiatives and community engagement. The University promotes biodiversity conservation, responsible management of soil and water resources, green campus practices and sustainable use of natural resources. Faculty and students participate in activities related to plantation, water conservation, waste management and environmental awareness, contributing to healthier and more resilient local ecosystems. Through academic initiatives and community outreach, the University continues to encourage responsible environmental stewardship and sustainable resource management.

blocks.text: 14.5.1 Minimizing alteration of aquatic ecosystems (plan)
Plan for Minimizing Alteration of Aquatic Ecosystems

Kalinga University is committed to minimizing adverse impacts on aquatic ecosystems through responsible water management, pollution prevention, biodiversity conservation and sustainable campus development. The University shall implement the following measures:
Key Actions
Protect water bodies by preventing unauthorized dumping, wastewater discharge and other activities that may degrade aquatic environments.
Control water pollution through appropriate treatment and responsible disposal of sewage, laboratory wastewater, chemicals and solid waste.
Conserve freshwater resources through rainwater harvesting, efficient water use and reuse of treated wastewater wherever feasible.
Maintain natural drainage systems and avoid unnecessary alteration or blockage of drainage channels.
Protect aquatic biodiversity by promoting native vegetation and preventing activities that disturb aquatic habitats.
Monitor water quality periodically to identify pollution or ecological deterioration and initiate corrective measures.
Promote awareness among students, faculty, staff and campus service providers regarding aquatic ecosystem conservation.
Integrate environmental considerations into campus development so that construction and infrastructure activities minimize impacts on water bodies and natural drainage.
Encourage research and student projects focusing on water conservation, aquatic pollution, biodiversity and ecosystem restoration.
Review the plan periodically and strengthen conservation measures based on monitoring results.
Responsibility
The University Administration, Environmental Sustainability Committee and relevant academic, engineering and maintenance departments shall coordinate implementation and monitoring of this plan.
Event- World Wetland Day 2026 Celebration
Time of event: 10:00 AM onwards
Mode of event: offline
Venue: Nandanvan Jungle Safari, Naya Raipur
No. of Participants: 85 students and 4 faculty members

Programme Objective: To raise awareness about the importance of wetlands in maintaining ecological balance, conserving biodiversity, and supporting sustainable livelihoods. The programme aimed to promote wetland and wildlife conservation, highlight the role of traditional knowledge and conservation practices in protecting wetland ecosystems, and provide students with practical experience through safaris and interactive sessions while encouraging the participation of both local and international students.

Programme Description: The Department of Zoology and the Green Club of Kalinga University, in collaboration with Nandanvan Jungle Safari and the Chhattisgarh Forest & Climate Change Department, organized an educational visit and safari programme to observe World Wetlands Day 2026. The event featured an informative ranger interaction and awareness session conducted by Mr. Vijay Patil (Forest Ranger) and supported by Mr. Upendra Sahu (Forest Department Member). This session highlighted the ecological importance of wetlands, wildlife conservation, and biodiversity management. A total of 85 students (including 24 African students) participated, enjoying a jungle safari where they observed diverse wildlife in their natural habitats and compared Indian fauna with ecosystems from their home countries. The event successfully fostered multicultural learning and environmental responsibility, concluding with a vote of thanks by Dr. Manoj Singh.

Coordinator(s): Dr. Manoj Singh (Head of the Department of Zoology & Green Club Coordinator) and Dr. Ajay Kumar Harit (Associate Professor & Green Club Coordinator), Department of Zoology & Green Club, Kalinga University

14.5.2 Monitoring the health of aquatic ecosystems

Kalinga University actively promotes the monitoring and conservation of aquatic ecosystems through field studies, academic research and student-led environmental initiatives. Periodic assessment of water-quality parameters such as pH, TDS, turbidity and other relevant indicators helps in understanding the condition of local water resources. Faculty and students also undertake studies related to aquatic biodiversity, pollution sources and human impacts on freshwater ecosystems. These efforts support informed conservation practices, sustainable management of water resources and the long-term protection of aquatic ecosystem health.
14.5.3 Programmes towards good aquatic stewardship practices

Kalinga University promotes aquatic stewardship through ongoing awareness, water conservation and environmental programmes involving students, faculty and local communities. Activities include water-quality awareness, responsible water use, aquatic ecosystem conservation, waste reduction and field-based environmental studies. Students and faculty participate in monitoring and awareness activities that encourage protection of freshwater resources and responsible management of aquatic environments. These programmes strengthen environmental awareness, community participation and sustainable water-management practices across and around the University.
Event: World River Day Celebration
Location: New Building, Kalinga University, Naya Raipur, Chhattisgarh
Date of the Event: 24 September 2025
No. of Participants: 37 NCC cadets participated in the programme.
Programme Objective:

To create awareness among students about river conservation, cleanliness, and the ecological, cultural, and economic importance of rivers. The programme aimed to sensitize cadets towards river pollution, promote sustainable water-resource management, and encourage responsibility for protecting rivers and aquatic ecosystems.
Programme Description:

The NCC Army Wing of Kalinga University organized World River Day under the Puneet Sagar Abhiyan and the theme “#Hamari Nadiya – Hamari Zimmedari (Cleaning & Protecting Rivers – Cradle of Civilization & Lifeline)”. The offline programme included a poster-making and awareness drive through which 37 cadets promoted messages on river cleanliness, water conservation, pollution control, and environmental sustainability. The activity encouraged teamwork, creativity, environmental stewardship, and youth participation in river and aquatic ecosystem conservation. The programme was aligned with SDGs 6, 13, 14, and 15.Coordinator(s):
Lt. Vibha Chandrakar, Assistant Professor, FD Department; In-charge, DSW; ANO, NCC Army Wing.
14.5.4 Collaboration for shared aquatic ecosystems

Kalinga University encourages collaboration with local communities and relevant institutions for the conservation and sustainable management of shared aquatic ecosystems. Faculty and students participate in awareness, water conservation, water-quality assessment and environmental activities involving local stakeholders. These collaborative efforts promote community participation in protecting nearby ponds, wetlands and other freshwater resources, while supporting pollution prevention, biodiversity conservation and responsible use of shared aquatic ecosystems.
14.5.5 Watershed management strategy
Kalinga University follows an integrated approach to watershed management with emphasis on conservation, efficient water use and protection of local water resources.
Key Strategies:
Rainwater Harvesting: Promote rainwater harvesting and storage to reduce surface runoff and enhance water availability.
Groundwater Recharge: Encourage recharge measures to support sustainable groundwater levels.
Water Conservation: Promote efficient use of water across academic, residential and other campus facilities.
Drainage Management: Protect natural drainage channels and reduce unnecessary alteration of drainage systems.
Soil and Erosion Control: Promote vegetation cover and suitable measures to reduce soil erosion and sedimentation.
Water Pollution Prevention: Ensure proper wastewater and solid-waste management to prevent contamination of water resources.
Vegetation Conservation: Protect green areas and vegetation surrounding water bodies to support watershed stability.
GIS and Field Studies: Use spatial analysis, drainage mapping and field surveys to identify watershed conditions and vulnerable areas.
Community Participation: Encourage local communities and stakeholders to participate in water conservation and watershed protection activities.
Monitoring and Assessment: Periodically assess water availability, quality and environmental conditions to improve watershed management measures.
Institutional Collaboration: Promote collaboration with government agencies, environmental organizations and local stakeholders for sustainable watershed management.
